statement: What is the minimal size of a context-free grammar of the word problem of a finite group?
context: Is the doubly exponential bound n12·2 +10 on the size of finite subgroups tight or is there a bound 2p(n) for some polynomial p? This is closely related to another question: What is the minimal size of a context-free grammar of the word problem of a finite group? Can it be log log(n) where n is the size of the group? Is there a polynomial bound on the number of slide moves necessary to transform two graphs of groups with isomorphic fundamental groups into each? This would lead to an NP algorithm for the isomorphism problem with virtually free presentations as input. We conjecture, however, that this is not true.
